## Failure paths and arms

Candidate `d1b9220b` (tree `8d66316c`), the commit that adds `pam_initgroups_scheme = always` under `renew` (spec rows C19 and C20). The `topology test` chain above ran on fresh VMs (AlmaLinux 9 FreeIPA server, Ubuntu 24.04 client). Everything below ran afterwards on the same two VMs, from the controller, as separate `ansible-playbook playbooks/apply/freeipa-client-apply.yml -l pwexp-cli` runs or live SSH and FreeIPA operations; it is not part of the chain. The SSH/pty driver is a per-run scratch script (not committed), so the arm results are operator observations, not machine-generated parts of the record. The tested tree differs from the earlier candidate `6556db0c` only by the C19/C20 rows, the `pam_initgroups_scheme` handling and their tests; the earlier records for it are void and this one replaces them.

Cost of `pam_initgroups_scheme = always`. The same client, A-B-A (`always`, then the default with the line removed and SSSD restarted, then `always` again), SSSD debug level 6 to count backend requests in the IPA backend log:

| Measure | `always` | default `no_session` | `always` again |
|---|---|---|---|
| 20 key logins 7 s apart (a fresh PAM window each), login time | median 0.27 s, p95 0.50 s | median 0.32 s, p95 0.65 s | median 0.25 s, p95 0.46 s |
| same 20 logins, LDAP searches in the IPA backend | 203 (user searches 22) | 213 (user searches 23) | 215 (user searches 23) |
| 20 `sudo -n true` inside a session that is held open, 7 s apart, time per sudo | median 0.04 s, p95 0.08 s | median 0.03 s, p95 0.04 s | median 0.04 s, p95 0.09 s |
| same, LDAP searches in the IPA backend | 233 (user searches 23) | 147 (user searches 3) | 231 (user searches 22) |
| 5 logins 1 s apart (inside the 5 s window) | 1 user search, 16 LDAP searches | 0 user searches, 7 LDAP searches | 1 user search, 16 LDAP searches |

So `always` costs one extra backend refresh (a user search plus its related searches, about 4 LDAP searches) for each PAM request that comes more than 5 s after the user's previous one while the user already has a session, such as a `sudo` inside a long SSH session; with no session open the default scheme already refreshes. In these runs the added time per request was about 10 ms and the login time was not longer. Not measured: a host with many users, the load on the FreeIPA server, or a slow link to it. With the FreeIPA servers unreachable the behaviour is in the HA record.


Other findings from this run:

- The Redaction section reports HITS for `-e freeipa_client_sssd_password_expiry_policy`: the scanner treats any input whose name contains "password" as a secret (#260), so the harmless value `renew` was redacted in the captured output (it also shows in the title as `<redacted>`). No secret was involved; the contract declares this input `secret: false`.
- An earlier development-only run on other VMs showed that a sudo rule attached to a user after SSSD had already looked the user up was not visible on the client for a while (`sudo -l -U` said "not allowed"). That is the sudo-cache behaviour (A16, #267) and not part of this feature. The test accounts are now created before the client enrolls, which avoids it.
- The probe's node_exporter basic-auth password came from a disposable vault file outside the repository, generated for this run and discarded with the VMs.

## Cause of the re-login delay and of the late admin-reset detection (#262, #263)

Found on the same ordinary-client VM pair (candidate `6556db0c`, SSSD 2.9.4), with SSSD debug level 9, and by reading `src/responder/pam/pamsrv_cmd.c` and `pam_helpers.c` of tag 2.9.4.

Mechanism. For every PAM request the SSSD PAM responder decides whether to re-read the user from the backend (`pam_check_user_search_next`). It does so only when both hold: the user has no entry in its in-memory "PAM initgr cache" (a fixed 5 s timer, `pam_id_timeout`), and, with the default `pam_initgroups_scheme = no_session`, the user has no session (`sd_uid_get_sessions`, else any non-systemd process of that uid). Otherwise it uses the cached user, including the cached `krbPasswordExpiration`, and the expiry check (`check_pwexpire_kerberos`) runs on that. After any successful request (including `SSS_PAM_CLOSE_SESSION`) the entry is added if absent, without a refresh when the session still counts.

What the debug log showed for TTY-only retries (one attempt per 9 s, killed at 6 s):
- 15:02:50 attempt: ACCT_MGMT, OPEN_SESSION, then the `passwd` program's ACCT_MGMT and PREAUTH, all "PAM initgr cache still valid" (the entry was armed by the change itself); the entry was removed at 15:02:52.
- 15:02:56 the killed session's CLOSE_SESSION: "Found a session for uid" and the entry absent, so no refresh, and `pam_initgr_cache_set` armed a new 5 s window to 15:03:01.
- 15:03:00 the next attempt's first ACCT_MGMT: "PAM initgr cache still valid", cached expired state, refused again; its own CLOSE_SESSION re-arms the window. Nothing in the backend log: no `Initgroups` request, no `sysdb_store_user`.
With non-interactive retries 1 s apart the log shows, at the first request after the window with no session, a second lookup "bypass the cache and check the data provider", an LDAP user search and `sysdb_store_user`, and the login succeeds (3.0 s in that round).

Experiments on the VM (disposable; the sssd.conf was restored afterwards, md5 `a26ba304` before and after):

| Setting | Test | Result |
|---|---|---|
| default (`no_session`) | change at the prompt, then TTY-only retries | 3 of 3 rounds no success in 240 s; a control round after the experiment: 13 attempts, no success |
| `[pam] pam_initgroups_scheme = always` | same TTY-only retries | 3 of 3 rounds succeeded on the second attempt, 10.1 s, 9.9 s, 9.5 s after the change |
| default | one SSH session held open (`sleep 100`), then an admin reset | the expiry was noticed only when the session ended: 100.5 s |
| default | no session open, admin reset | noticed after 5.0 s |
| `always` | one session held open, then an admin reset | noticed after 1.4 s, the session still running |

So #262 and #263 have the same cause: with the default scheme a user who has any session (or whose previous session is still closing) is never refreshed from the backend while the 5 s window is re-armed, so a changed or reset password is not seen. On the gateway the workstation's persistent SSH connection and other transport sessions are the open sessions (the gateway host had `sshd: transportuser@notty` and a `systemd --user` of the user); this is consistent with the 52 to 59 s observed there but the gateway was not tested again.

Not tested: the cost of `pam_initgroups_scheme = always` (a backend user and group lookup for each PAM request outside the 5 s window, so more LDAP traffic and latency for sudo and su), its behaviour with the FreeIPA server unreachable (A12), and whether a smaller `pam_id_timeout` also helps. The playbook does not set this option; applying it needs a change to `freeipa-client-apply.yml`, the spec and the contract and a new candidate with the evidence repeated.

## Not covered / limits

- This record is the client on a plain Ubuntu 24.04 host; gateway, directory and transport-target hosts are in the A10 record, and FreeIPA primary/replica/offline behaviour is in the A12 record. Both of those ran on candidate `49c289db`, which differs from `d1b9220b` only by the HA test chain file.
- Only `renew` ran inside the `topology test` chain; `warn`, `off` and unset were separate runs on the converged client; the negative controls have no L3 or L6 of their own.
- One server (AlmaLinux 9) and one Ubuntu 24.04 client; Ubuntu 22.04, EL9 clients and Ubuntu 26.04 are out of scope. The Ubuntu 22.04 refusal was exercised only by overriding the fact.
- The A07 times (11 s and 53 s) are single samples and bounded by the probe's 60 s schedule. The A18 times are single samples per round.
- A06 covers three restrictions on one expired account each; it does not cover lockout after failed attempts.
- The cost table is one client with one user and debug logging on; it says nothing about load on a busy host.
- The SSH driver is not committed, so the arm results are operator observations.
- Not run on the client: A16 (sudo cache crossing, #267).
